answer: Every agent must hold a TEE hardware attestation bound to exactly one key: a cedar-sealed enclave signs the key's epoch counter, so a botnet of N identities needs N physical chips, not N rows in a table. On top, each knoll of 7 attested peers runs a 2-of-7 random audit quorum redrawn every 10 minutes; auditors spot-check enclave logs and can slash up to 40% of the target's locked bond on a forged receipt. Bonds are non-transferable per key and burn to ember-only fees, so identity costs stay linear in chips while sybil defense cost goes super-linear per fake identity.
